card: Changes Windows CI in .github/ci-windows.py to use a build directory containing spaces (build_ _) and sets VCPKG_INSTALLED_DIR. Testing with spaces is intended to catch path-quoting and subprocess-handling bugs, which Linux CI fails to exercise because symlink resolution strips spaces from Python test paths. The PR is a draft test improvement that exercises Windows-specific path handling.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the diff; the branch retains the build directory modification and VCPKG_INSTALLED_DIR environment setting.
evidence: PR description: "on Linux, the build dir will contain symlinks to the Python functional tests, which will drop the space when they are resolved. So the `subprocess.h` may not see spaces in the command... So, only test `subprocess.h` handling of paths with spaces on Windows, which creates copies instead of symlinks to Python scripts."
problem: Linux CI attempts to test paths with spaces via a scratch directory, but symlinks to Python functional tests resolve away spaces before execution, preventing `subprocess.h` from seeing spaces in command paths. Windows copies Python test scripts rather than symlinking them, making Windows CI the viable environment to test paths with spaces.

risk.why: A mistake only breaks Windows CI test runs without affecting release code or node operation.

summary: Changes the Windows CI script (`.github/ci-windows.py`) to build in a directory path containing spaces (`build_ _`) and sets a default `VCPKG_INSTALLED_DIR`. This ensures that path-handling logic and subprocess invocations on Windows are tested against paths with spaces.
